messages.content: Help me create a MethodEntryRequest for a specific thread `mainThread`, class `com.example.MainClass`, with a suspend policy of `EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL`, and a custom property `testProperty` in a JDI test environment?

function.name: filter_s002_setting22MethodEntryRequest
function.description: Sets up a MethodEntryRequest with specified thread filter, class filter, suspend policy, and custom property. Throws JDITestRuntimeException on failure. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

thread.description: The ThreadReference to which the request will be applied. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

testedClass.description: The name of the class to filter for method entries. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

suspendPolicy.description: The suspend policy to be used for this request. This is Java integer type parameter in string representation.

property.description: A custom property to associate with this request. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

message.reasoning:
The user wants help creating a MethodEntryRequest for a specific thread mainThread, class com.example.MainClass, suspend policy EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL, custom property testProperty. They want to use the function filter_s002_setting22MethodEntryRequest. We need to call it with appropriate arguments. The function expects thread as string representation of Java object. So we pass "mainThread". testedClass: "com.example.MainClass". suspendPolicy: "EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL" or maybe numeric value? In Java, EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL is an int constant. But they say it's Java integer type parameter in string representation. So we should pass the string representation of the integer value. EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL is 2? Actually in JDI, EventRequest.SUSPEND_NONE=0, SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD=1, SUSPEND_ALL=2. So we could pass "2". But the user might expect "EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL". The function signature says suspendPolicy: string. It says "This is Java integer type parameter in string representation." So likely we should pass "2". But we can also pass "EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL"? That would not be integer. So better to pass "2". For property: "testProperty".

Thus we call:

{
  thread: "mainThread",
  testedClass: "com.example.MainClass",
  suspendPolicy: "2",
  property: "testProperty"
}

We then output the function call.
